problem: Ashley has $5$ tasks. She decides to do one on Thursday and another on Friday. How many different choices of the two tasks does Ashley have?

feedback.problem: Diana is choosing a $4$-digit passcode for her cellphone from the digits ${1,2,3,4,5,6},$ where no digit is used more than once. How many different passcodes are possible?
feedback.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $6$ digits, so $n=6.$ We want to select $4$ of those digits for the passcode, so we have $r=4.$ 

Therefore, the number of different passcodes is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{6}{P}_{4} & =\frac{6!}{(6-4)!} \\  & =\frac{6!}{2!} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot \cancel{2!}}{\cancel{2!}} \\  & =6\cdot 5\cdot 4\cdot 3 \\  & =360.\end{aligned}
$$
